story_type: arresting cable parts during a carrier landing, plane rolls off the deck and flies away
hook: The cable broke. The plane rolled right off the carrier.
narration: The cable broke, and this Navy plane rolled straight off the end of the carrier.
It was an E-2C Hawkeye, landing on the USS Dwight D. Eisenhower off the coast of Virginia.
A routine landing, during carrier qualifications.
A hook on the tail catches a steel cable stretched across the deck, and that cable stops the plane in about two seconds.
This time, the arresting gear parted while the Hawkeye was still rolling.
The plane dropped off the edge of the deck and out of sight.
Then it came back into view, climbing away from the ship.
outcome: The Hawkeye regained flight and returned safely to its base at Naval Station Norfolk.
title: Carrier cable snapped mid landing
description:
On March 18, 2016, an arresting gear parted during a routine landing by an E-2C Hawkeye aboard the USS Dwight D. Eisenhower off the Virginia coast. The aircraft regained flight and returned safely to Naval Station Norfolk.
